segments: The seventh discourse: The Arab Kings.
They dressed him in a mean tunic of the scullery boys,
and they placed a cooking table {pot-tray} upon his head,
and brought him out in the evening from the palace,
and mounted him on a horse,
and in one night they brought him to Caesarea,
and set him on the throne,
and a multitude of his troops gathered to him.
And Rukn al-Din led them,
and came to wage war with his brother 'Izz al-Din.
And 'Izz al-Din went out, encountered him, and broke him again,
and captured him, and imprisoned him in the fortress called Dawalu.
And in the year 1566
[1566 of the Greeks?]
which is the year 653
Shirkuh
that is,
Lion Mountain [Mountain Lion?],
and Rukn al-Din his son arose after him.
And Hulagu sent and said to him:
"If your intention is right with us, and you desire reconciliation and peace,
destroy all your fortresses,
and you personally come to us;
otherwise, prepare yourself for war."
Rukn al-Din quickly sent and destroyed five fortresses of those in which there was no strength,
and which were not able to hold out before the Tatars.
And he sent a reply to Hulagu:
"Behold, in part I have fulfilled {OCR?} your command,
and little by little I will demolish the rest of the fortresses."
Hulagu, however, knew that he was seeking to let the days pass by craftiness;
therefore he sent Kitbuqa against the fortress called Shahdayr [Shahdiz?],
and in two days he captured it,
and three other fortresses around it.
Then Rukn al-Din took one of the sons of the poor,
and clothed him in royal robes,
and sent him to the emir king.
Hulagu, although he knew that he was a common foot-soldier's son,
did not show it,
but sent him back with honor,
and said:
"It was you I wanted,
and not your son."
And again afterward he sent his true brother, whose name was Shiranshah, with three hundred horsemen.
And Hulagu, while seizing the horsemen and sending them to Qazwin,
sent his brother back to him and said
that he himself should come.
And on the night of the Savior's Nativity,
as he rose to come to the service,
his servants drew knives against him and said:
"If you go, we will kill you."
Then he sent and made the matter known to the King of Kings.
